transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My thoughts won’t slow down, and it’s gotten to the point where I can’t focus enough to do my work safely. I'm an apprentice pipefitter, and things got so bad on the job site that I had to step back and get some help.
Have you been sleeping much less than usual without feeling tired, or felt unusually energized, overly confident, or more talkative than normal?

Yes, during those "up" stretches, I feel incredibly energized and barely sleep, staying awake until 3 or 4 AM with my brain buzzing. I get so confident that I honestly feel like I'm the only one who really gets our piping system and want to redesign the whole thing myself. I also talk so fast and constantly about all my ideas that people literally have to cut me off because I just can't stop.

Have you ever had a major depressive episode in the past, with at least two weeks of feeling very down or losing interest in things, or have your symptoms only ever happened during these high-energy periods?

Yes, I definitely get those heavy, low periods too, and they've actually been dragging on for about nine months now. I feel so drained and guilty that I've completely lost interest in my pipefitting work and stopped showing up for the kids at the community center. It's like a constant cloud where I just can't bring myself to care about anything.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever heard or seen things that other people could not, or felt like you had special powers or a mission that others thought was unrealistic?

No, I’ve never seen or heard things that weren’t actually there. But when I'm in those high periods, I absolutely feel like I'm on a special mission, convinced we are building something historic and that I'm the only one who truly understands the system. I genuinely believed I could single-handedly redesign the entire downtown Miami water setup and get featured in a magazine.

During your high-energy periods, do you ever lose touch with reality—for example, hearing or seeing things that aren’t there, or having beliefs that other people clearly say are impossible or bizarre?

No, I don't hear or see things that aren't there. But I do get intense beliefs that others find unrealistic, like thinking I can single-handedly redesign the entire downtown Miami water setup to get featured in magazines. And if people don't agree with my ideas, I can suddenly flip to feeling like everyone is against me.

During your high-energy periods, do you ever believe things that are clearly impossible or not based in reality, even when other people strongly disagree with you? For example, feeling certain you have special powers, a unique mission, or that you can do things far beyond normal human ability.

I don't think I have literal magical powers or anything impossible like that, but I definitely get extremely overconfident. During those high stretches, I was convinced I was the only one on the crew who truly understood the system we were installing, and that I could redesign the entire downtown Miami water setup and get featured in a magazine.
During your high-energy periods, do you ever become absolutely certain of beliefs that are clearly impossible or obviously untrue, even when others strongly disagree with you?

I don't think my ideas are completely impossible or crazy, but I do get extremely confident in things that others might find highly unrealistic. During my high stretches, I honestly believed I was the only one on the crew who truly understood the system we were installing. I was convinced I could redesign the entire downtown Miami water setup myself and get featured in a magazine.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or beliefs that were clearly impossible or bizarre, even after other people told you they were not true?

No, I've never experienced hallucinations or seen and heard things that aren't there. While I do get highly overconfident and have some really big ideas, I don't believe things that are completely impossible or bizarre.
During your high-energy periods, do your beliefs ever become clearly untrue or bizarre even when other people strongly disagree, or do they stay more like extreme confidence and big ideas?

They definitely stay more like extreme confidence and big ideas. During my high stretches, I get convinced that I'm the only one on the crew who truly understands the system we're installing. I honestly believe that if they'd just let me run with my ideas, I could redesign the whole downtown Miami water setup and get featured in a magazine.
How long do your high-energy periods usually last, and have any of them lasted at least one week without stopping?

Yes, they definitely last for weeks at a time, and there were weeks where I would leave the job site wired every single day and stay up half the night. This whole rollercoaster of highs and crashes has been going on for about the last five months, ever since we started the big Miami project.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or become absolutely convinced of beliefs that were clearly impossible or bizarre, even when others strongly disagreed with you?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like hallucinations or bizarre, impossible beliefs, even when I feel really high-energy. It’s always just felt like extreme confidence and having way too many big ideas at once.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever become so suspicious, confused, or out of touch with reality that other people thought you were psychotic, even if you did not hear or see things?

No, I’ve never really experienced being out of touch with reality, and nobody has ever seen me as psychotic. Sometimes when my mood swings I do get defensive and feel like everyone is against me, but it has never gone that far.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or beliefs that were clearly impossible or bizarre, even when other people strongly disagreed with you?

No, I have never had hallucinations or believed in things that were completely impossible or bizarre. Even when I am feeling really high-energy, it is always just extreme confidence and big ideas, not losing touch with reality.
During your low periods, do you ever hear, see, or strongly believe things that other people say are not true, or has it only been mood changes without hallucinations or delusions?

No, I’ve never experienced hearing, seeing, or believing things that others say aren't real during my low periods. It has really just been about extreme mood drops, a total lack of energy, and having a lot of negative thoughts about myself.
During your high periods, do you ever have hallucinations or fixed beliefs that are clearly not true or impossible, even when other people strongly disagree?

No, I haven't really experienced seeing or hearing things that aren't there, or holding completely impossible beliefs. I do get extremely overconfident and sometimes feel like everyone is against me when I'm wound up, but it has never gone beyond that.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or become completely convinced of beliefs that were clearly not true, even when other people strongly disagreed with you?

No, I haven't experienced hallucinations or believed things that were completely untrue. I did have moments where I felt highly overconfident about my abilities on the job, but it never went beyond that.

During your high-energy periods, have you ever become so suspicious or convinced that others were plotting against you, or so certain of unrealistic ideas, that it felt like you were losing touch with reality?

I don't think I've lost touch with reality, but I do get really unrealistic ideas, like believing I could redesign the whole downtown Miami water setup myself. Also, when my mood swings, I can suddenly feel like everyone is against me and blow up over tiny things. But I've never actually seen or heard things that aren't there.
Have you ever had a manic episode where you were clearly out of touch with reality, such as having hallucinations or fixed delusions that other people said were impossible or obviously untrue?

No, I’ve never experienced hallucinations or fixed delusions where I felt completely out of touch with reality. I definitely get very overconfident and carried away with my grand ideas when my mood is high, but it has never gone beyond that.
During your low periods, do you ever feel so hopeless or guilty that you think about hurting yourself or that life is not worth living?

Yes, when I'm down, I constantly replay every mistake I've made on the Miami project and feel like a complete screw-up who doesn't deserve this apprenticeship. On the worst days, I've thought it would be easier if I just didn't wake up, and I've even looked at my pill bottles and planned how many it would take before I got scared enough to call off work and stay with my mom.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, with little interest or pleasure, and at the same time had hallucinations or fixed false beliefs?

Yes, I've definitely had a long period over the last nine months where I felt incredibly down, drained, and completely lost interest in welding and helping the kids at the community center. However, I have never experienced any hallucinations, heard or seen things that weren't there, or held fixed false beliefs during those times.
Have you ever had a time when your depression was so severe that you heard or saw things other people couldn’t, or became completely convinced of false beliefs that others said were not true?

No, I have never heard or seen things that weren't there, nor have I held beliefs that others found completely untrue or delusional, even during my worst depressive periods. It has really just been a very heavy, draining feeling of hopelessness and guilt.
During your worst depression, have you ever heard or seen things that weren’t there, or become completely convinced of things that others said were clearly untrue?

No, I have never experienced anything like that during my low periods. I've never heard or seen things that weren't there, and I've never held beliefs that others told me were untrue. For me, the depression has just been a very deep, heavy sadness and feeling completely worthless.
Have you ever had a period when your depression was so severe that you heard, saw, or became completely convinced of things that other people said were not true?
No, even when I've felt at my absolute lowest, I've never experienced seeing or hearing things that weren't there. I also haven't believed things that other people told me weren't true.
During your current low period, are you still able to do your daily activities like work, eating, and basic self-care, or have you become unable to function because of the depression?

My ability to function has completely broken down during these low periods, and I actually had to step back from my apprenticeship because I wasn't safe or reliable on the job site anymore. I've also stopped going to the community center and seeing friends because I just can't keep up with any plans. On my worst days, I will just stare at my tools or my phone for hours, unable to make myself care enough to do anything.
